source_review.notes: Checked all seven references for issuer, identity, version or date, and cited scope. NIST FIPS 186-5 supports signature integrity and signatory-authentication claims and its 2025 planning note; RFC 8032 supports Ed25519/Ed448 specification claims; TUF 1.0.28 supports role, threshold, expiry, rollback, delegation, and dual-threshold root rotation; current Sigstore security documentation supports short-lived identity certificates, transparency, monitoring, and explicit non-guarantees; DSSE 1.0 supports typed pre-authentication encoding; RFC 5280 supports certificate path validation; and RFC 9162 supports auditable Merkle-tree certificate transparency. Checked 2026-09-06.

evidence: Defined Gen, Sign, Verify, keys, message, signature, artifact digest, evidence, identity, scope, time evidence, and policy before use.
Checked probability, security parameter, set, intersection, cardinality, threshold inequality, conjunction, and all GitHub math delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The notation is scheme-neutral and deliberately separates cryptographic verification from delivery authorization.

evidence: Executed evaluate-signature-policy under CPython 3.14.4 and matched all seven exact Boolean outputs.
Recomputed the two-of-two accepted baseline and each one-variable rejection, including evidence epoch 41 below minimum 42 and two distinct authorized identities at epoch 43.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Epoch values are deterministic teaching data, not wall-clock or cryptographic timestamps.

evidence: Checked signature correctness does not imply the separately defined authorization predicate.
Checked the substitution argument under subject digest, byte-boundary, and collision-resistance assumptions.
Checked threshold acceptance uses distinct identities in the authorized-set intersection and that widening trust expands possible acceptances.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No signature unforgeability proof, hash injectivity, PKI correctness, or log consistency proof is claimed.

evidence: Reviewed wrong artifact, adjacent attacker key, payload confusion, mutable tag, overbroad issuer, wrong namespace, duplicate signer, and insufficient threshold cases.
Reviewed expired certificates, historical timestamps, revocation, signer compromise, root rotation, rollback, freeze, offline clients, emergency recovery, and lost trust material.
Reviewed compromised workloads, exposed keys, log omission or forks, unmonitored identities, privacy leakage, detached and embedded signatures, and multi-artifact manifests.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Cryptographic algorithm and key-management decisions require current security review and system-specific threat models.

evidence: Traced independent trust roots, exact subject binding, domain separation, maintained crypto, certificate constraints, exact authorization, signer isolation, distinct thresholds, time evidence, transparency monitoring, and rotation history through examples and answers.
Checked that signatures, certificates, logs, timestamps, provenance, and deployment approval retain separate meanings.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter defines delivery-verification invariants but does not certify any signer, CA, log, update repository, or artifact.

evidence: Reviewed the substitution argument and confirmed it depends on recomputation and cryptographic digest assumptions.
Reviewed the threshold condition for distinct authorized identities and rejected repeated signatures from one identity.
Reviewed trust-widening monotonicity as a set-inclusion property while noting other policy changes can interact.
proof_review.notes: This is internal proof review of bounded abstract claims, not formal cryptographic, PKI, TUF, Sigstore, or transparency-log verification.

evidence: Audited uses of proof, argument, invariant, authentic, authorized, trusted, valid, current, safe, correct, included, and immutable.
Confirmed standards statements, conditional deductions, hypothetical attacks, local policy-model results, and professional recommendations remain distinct.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No artifact safety, non-repudiation guarantee, signer honesty, universal freshness, log honesty, or external review is claimed.

evidence: Executed the sole practical snippet under CPython 3.14.4 with exact stdout, empty stderr, and exit status zero.
Confirmed signing, PKI, transparency, repository, compromise, and offline-device cases are hypothetical teaching scenarios.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Local execution performs set and policy checks only; it explicitly reports cryptography_executed=False and performs no hashing, signature, certificate, time, revocation, or log verification.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed message construction, domain separation, artifact binding, roots, identity, authorization, thresholds, signer placement, time, revocation, transparency, update freshness, rotation, compromise response, and evidence retention as one bounded foundational signing chapter.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed failures across attacker-supplied keys, subject substitution, ambiguous payloads, broad issuers, exposed workload keys, duplicate authorities, expired evidence, moved tags, unmonitored logs, compromised signers, root rotation, rollback, and disconnected devices. Controls are actionable. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified undergraduate progression from signature semantics through a conjunctive acceptance model, three bounded formal arguments, one executable seven-outcome policy checker, fifteen misconceptions, ten distinct examples, and five exercises progressing from guarantees through trace, diagnosis, governance design, and offline-device transfer.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, executable-policy, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, cryptographic, or practitioner review is claimed. Standards, abstract arguments, one local non-cryptographic execution, and internal review do not establish algorithm security, key custody, signer honesty, PKI validity, log consistency, artifact safety, deployment authorization, or production conformance.
